ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is a power supply marked 10V; its upper end is connected by a wire to switch position 1, and its lower end is connected to the ground point through a 100Ω resistor. The moving terminal of the switch is connected to the upper plate of a 6µF capacitor, and the lower plate of the 6µF capacitor is grounded. Switch position 2 is connected to the left plate of a 15µF capacitor, and the node where the right plate of the 15µF capacitor is located is marked as point 3. Point 3 is further connected through a 10µF capacitor to the lower node, and this lower node is grounded through a 200Ω resistor. Reasoning: When the switch is first connected to position 1 and reaches steady state, the capacitors are equivalent to open circuits, and there is no DC current through the 100Ω, so the lower end of the power supply is at ground potential, and position 1 is +10V. The lower plate of the 6µF capacitor is grounded and the upper plate is connected to +10V, so the charge on its upper plate is Q=CV=6µF×10V=60µC. At this time the 15µF and 10µF capacitors are not charged. After the switch is moved to position 2 and reaches a new steady state, there is no DC current in the 200Ω, so the lower end of the 10µF capacitor is ultimately at ground potential. Let the potential of the isolated node consisting of the switch moving terminal/position 2/15µF left plate/6µF upper plate be Va, and the potential of point 3 be V3. Conservation of charge for the isolated node Va: 6Va + 15(Va−V3)=60. Conservation of charge for the isolated conductor where point 3 is located: 15(V3−Va)+10V3=0. The second equation gives 25V3=15Va, namely V3=0.6Va. Substitute into the first equation: 6Va+15Va−15V3=60, namely 21Va−15(0.6Va)=60, so 12Va=60, Va=5V, therefore V3=3V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, the switch is first connected to position 1 and, after the circuit stabilizes, it is connected to position 2. When the circuit stabilizes again, what is the potential at point 3?

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology. With the switch at position 1 for a long time, the 6 µF capacitor charges to 10 V because its bottom plate is grounded and its top plate is connected to the 10 V node; hence the switch-wiper conductor initially carries +60 µC on the top plate. The 15 µF and 10 µF capacitors are initially uncharged. After switching to position 2 and waiting, the lower node of the 10 µF capacitor is at ground because no DC current flows through the 200 Ω resistor. Let Va be the final voltage of the switch/contact-2/left-15µF/top-6µF node, and V3 be the voltage at point 3. Conserve charge on the isolated node Va: 6Va + 15(Va−V3)=60. Conserve charge on the isolated point-3 conductor: 15(V3−Va)+10V3=0. Solve these two equations to obtain Va=5 V and V3=3 V.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左侧有一个标为 10V 的电源，上端通过导线接到开关位置 1，下端经 100Ω 电阻接到接地点。开关的动端连接到一个 6µF 电容的上极板，6µF 电容下极板接地。开关位置 2 连接到一个 15µF 电容的左极板，15µF 电容右极板所在节点标为点 3。点 3 再通过一个 10µF 电容接到下方节点，该下方节点经 200Ω 电阻接地。

推理：开关先接位置 1 并达到稳态时，电容相当于断路，100Ω 上无直流电流，因此电源下端为地电位，位置 1 为 +10V。6µF 电容下极板接地、上极板接 +10V，所以其上极板电荷为 Q=CV=6µF×10V=60µC。此时 15µF 和 10µF 电容未被充电。

开关转到位置 2 后达到新稳态，200Ω 中无直流电流，所以 10µF 电容下端最终为地电位。设开关动端/位置2/15µF左极板/6µF上极板这一孤立节点电位为 Va，点 3 电位为 V3。对孤立节点 Va 守恒电荷：6Va + 15(Va−V3)=60。对点 3 所在孤立导体守恒电荷：15(V3−Va)+10V3=0。第二式给出 25V3=15Va，即 V3=0.6Va。代入第一式：6Va+15Va−15V3=60，即 21Va−15(0.6Va)=60，所以 12Va=60，Va=5V，因此 V3=3V。

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology. In the initial stable state with the switch at 1, only the 6 µF capacitor is charged to 10 V, so its isolated top-node charge is Q0=6 µF×10 V=60 µC. In the final stable state at position 2, treat the network seen from the switch node to ground as a 6 µF capacitor in parallel with the series combination of 15 µF and 10 µF, because the bottom of the 10 µF capacitor is effectively at ground through the 200 Ω resistor. The series capacitance is (15×10)/(15+10)=6 µF, so the total capacitance from the conserved switch node to ground is 6+6=12 µF. Therefore the final switch-node voltage is 60 µC/12 µF=5 V. The charge in the 15 µF–10 µF series branch is 6 µF×5 V=30 µC, so the voltage across the 10 µF capacitor, i.e. point 3 relative to ground, is 30 µC/10 µF=3 V.

The second equation gives 25V3=15Va, namely V3=0.6Va. Substitute into the first equation: 6Va+15Va−15V3=60, namely 21Va−15(0.6Va)=60, so 12Va=60, Va=5V, therefore V3=3V.
